prompt: Turn a name-to-score map inside out. Complete the invert method so it returns a map from each score to the alphabetically sorted list of names that earned it.
explanation: Inverting a map whose values repeat means each output value must be a collection, so the result type is Map<Integer, List<String>>. Iterating scores.entrySet() gives each name-score pair, and computeIfAbsent creates the list for a score the first time it is seen before adding the name to it. A final pass sorts every list with Collections.sort so the grouping order never depends on the input map's iteration order.
hints: Loop over scores.entrySet(); for each entry the VALUE becomes the new key and the KEY joins a list.
result.computeIfAbsent(score, k -> new ArrayList<>()).add(name) creates the list on first use and appends in one line.
After grouping, loop over result.values() and Collections.sort each list to get alphabetical order.
